question.problem: Which of the following gives the total area enclosed by graph of the polar curve $r=9\theta +5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}?$

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217747/assets/d7b39805131dc562e233d49a84f69d30e80ca29cb9443012032d18fdb4512054.png)

Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r = 2\sin\theta + 2\cos\theta$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \leq \theta \leq \dfrac{3\pi}{4},$ as shown above.
current_example.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} r^2(\theta) \, \textrm{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta) = 2\sin\theta + 2\cos\theta,$ $\theta_1=\dfrac{\pi}{2},$ and $\theta_2=\dfrac{3\pi}{4},$ this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(4+8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{4}{2}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2(\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{2}\,{|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}) \\  & =2\theta \,{|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =2(\frac{3\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}-1 \\  & =\frac{\pi -2}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
